title: LDL as a causal risk factor; risk assessment context
tags: LDL-C ASCVD Mendelian randomization risk assessment family history GISSI-2
summary: LDL-C causality for ASCVD rests on genetics, cohort studies and randomized trials. Risk equations underperform when family history and lipoprotein-specific risk are not captured; an early-onset MI in first-degree relatives carries a markedly higher MI risk. CAC can reclassify risk upward or downward.

title: High-risk and very-high-risk ASCVD definitions (2018 AHA/ACC) — superseded
tags: very high risk recent ACS stroke PAD high-risk conditions
summary: The textbook lists major ASCVD events (recent ACS, prior MI, ischaemic stroke, symptomatic PAD) and high-risk conditions (age>=65, HeFH, prior revascularization, diabetes, hypertension, CKD eGFR 15-59, smoking, persistent LDL-C>=100 on maximal therapy, heart failure). Very high risk = multiple major events or one major event plus multiple high-risk conditions. Replaced by the 2026 ACC/AHA guideline.

title: Residual risk after MI and by vascular territory
tags: residual risk polyvascular CKD diabetes heart failure
summary: Even with intensive medical therapy after MI, recurrent-event risk is high, roughly doubled with prior CHD, diabetes and CKD; event rates rise with the number of vascular beds involved.

title: Hypercholesterolaemia: definition, prevalence, severity thresholds
tags: LDL-C 190 severe 1 in 20 biochemical levels
summary: About 1 in 20 people have hypercholesterolaemia (>95th percentile). Mild-moderate LDL-C 130-189 mg/dL is mostly polygenic plus secondary factors; severe >=190 mg/dL suggests a monogenic disorder and/or marked polygenic load. TG mild-moderate 200-999, severe >=1000 mg/dL; low HDL-C 25-35 mild, <25 severe (textbook thresholds).

title: Secondary causes of dyslipidaemia and investigations
tags: secondary hypothyroidism nephrotic cholestasis drugs diabetes alcohol TSH creatinine
summary: Raised LDL-C: hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, obstructive liver disease, anorexia nervosa, high saturated/trans fat; drugs: cyclosporine, amiodarone, thiazides, high-dose chlorthalidone, rosiglitazone. Raised TG: obesity, alcohol, high carbohydrate, diabetes/insulin resistance, CKD, Cushing, HIV, SLE; oral oestrogens, tamoxifen, corticosteroids, beta-blockers, retinoids, protease inhibitors, bile acid resins, sirolimus, L-asparaginase, atypical antipsychotics. Work-up: creatinine/urea, glucose/HbA1c, TSH, urinalysis/24h albumin, AST/ALT/bilirubin/ALP. Treat the secondary cause first; persistent elevation implies an endogenous susceptibility.

title: Severe monogenic dyslipidaemias
tags: LDLR APOB PCSK9 LDLRAP1 LPL APOC2 APOA5 LMF1 GPIHBP1 ABCA1 LCAT APOA1
summary: High LDL-C: LDLR, APOB, PCSK9 (codominant), LDLRAP1 (recessive). Familial chylomicronaemia: LPL, APOC2, APOA5, LMF1, GPIHBP1, GPD1. Dysbetalipoproteinaemia: APOE. Low HDL-C: ABCA1 (Tangier), LCAT, APOA1.

title: FH clinical scoring systems and classification
tags: FH Simon Broome Dutch Lipid Clinic MED-PED classification genetic risk severe hypercholesterolaemia
summary: Simon Broome, DLCN, MED-PED, ICD-10 and Canadian criteria give 'possible' to 'definite' FH; a positive DNA test alone gives definite in SBR/DLCN. Four groups by LDL-C>=190 mg/dL and pathogenic variant: FH (~1:300-500; >20-fold ASCVD risk), severe hypercholesterolaemia without variant (~1:20; >5-fold), variant without high LDL-C (>2-fold), neither. Biochemical cascade screening applies to the first three; genetic cascade to those with a variant.

title: Genetics of FH, homozygous FH, other genes
tags: LDLR classes APOB familial defective apoB PCSK9 gain of function homozygous apheresis
summary: LDLR variants cause >=80% of genetically defined FH (six mutation classes); APOB binding-domain variants cause 5-10%; PCSK9 gain-of-function <1%. Genetic tests are interpreted with caution (computational prediction discordance up to ~50%). Homozygous FH (LDL-C 4-6x normal) is managed mainly by LDL-apheresis plus statin/ezetimibe and an empirical PCSK9 mAb trial.

title: Screening for FH: cascade vs universal
tags: cascade screening first-degree 50% second-degree 25% universal childhood
summary: Cascade screening tests first-degree relatives (50% chance of carrying the variant), then relatives of new cases; second/third degree 25%/12.5%. Universal childhood screening (e.g. at immunization) identified ~8 FH cases per 1000 in a pilot. Cascade depends on index-case identification and family acceptance.

title: Polygenic hypercholesterolaemia and combined hyperlipidaemia
tags: polygenic SNP combined hyperlipidemia CHL
summary: 20-40% of severe hypercholesterolaemia without an FH variant is polygenic. Combined hyperlipidaemia (LDL-C and TG >90th percentile) has no single gene; no dedicated guideline — apply principles from FH-equivalent LDL-C levels; TG component treated with weight loss and diet; adjunctive TG drugs on statin unproven apart from icosapent ethyl.

title: Other genetic dyslipidaemias mimicking FH
tags: sitosterolaemia LAL deficiency Lp(a) FH mimic
summary: Elevated Lp(a), sitosterolaemia (ABCG5/8) and lysosomal acid lipase deficiency (LIPA) are sometimes found in people with suspected FH.

title: Lifestyle and dietary management of hypercholesterolaemia
tags: diet Mediterranean DASH saturated fat trans fat soluble fibre plant sterols smoking alcohol
summary: Foundation of care: attain healthy weight, reduce overall intake and portions, replace high-glycaemic foods with complex carbohydrate, replace trans/saturated fat with unsaturated fat, add soluble fibre or plant sterols (after sitosterolaemia excluded), remove alcohol where TG high. Mediterranean/DASH patterns; culturally appropriate dietitian advice; control smoking, glycaemia and BP.

title: Drug therapy: monitoring and response
tags: statin 8 weeks titration switch ezetimibe PCSK9 algorithm
summary: Check response at about 8 weeks. If target not met: titrate, switch to a more potent statin, or add ezetimibe then a PCSK9 inhibitor. With adverse effects: dechallenge to confirm, switch statin, or move to ezetimibe/PCSK9 inhibitor. Algorithm shows LDL-C <70 target and <50 mg/dL for very high risk (2018-era).

title: Statins, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors, bile acid sequestrants, niacin
tags: atorvastatin rosuvastatin simvastatin pitavastatin evolocumab alirocumab colesevelam cholestyramine niacin
summary: Approx. LDL-C reductions: atorvastatin 35-50%, rosuvastatin 37-52%, simvastatin 32-46%, ezetimibe 18-25%, bile acid sequestrants 7-20%, PCSK9 mAbs 50-70%. Statins: strongest outcome evidence. Sequestrants raise TG (avoid TG >400 mg/dL). Niacin rarely used after trials showed no incremental benefit.

title: Newer LDL-lowering therapies and apheresis
tags: bempedoic acid inclisiran lomitapide mipomersen evinacumab apheresis gemcabene
summary: Bempedoic acid (ACL inhibitor): 15-20% monotherapy, up to 48% with ezetimibe (textbook, pre-outcome data). Lomitapide (MTP inhibitor) for HoFH: up to 40% LDL-C reduction with transaminase/hepatic fat risk. Mipomersen withdrawn 2019. Inclisiran, evinacumab listed with regional approvals as of the text. LDL-apheresis is the HoFH standard; also considered in refractory severe hypercholesterolaemia.

title: Children and adolescents with FH
tags: paediatric statin evolocumab specialist referral
summary: Diet/lifestyle first; statin timing in paediatric HeFH remains evolving; sequestrants poorly tolerated; limited ezetimibe data; evolocumab lowers LDL-C in adolescents. Refer to specialist.

title: Lp(a): structure, genetics, level distribution
tags: lipoprotein(a) apo(a) LPA kringle isoform ancestry
summary: Lp(a) is an LDL-like particle with apo(a) bound to apoB-100; levels are largely genetically determined (LPA, heritability >90%), stable through life, and vary by ancestry (South Asians have higher levels than Africans' ranges in some analyses; attributable MI risk highest in South Asians in one study). Smaller apo(a) isoforms give higher levels.

title: Lp(a) and cardiovascular disease
tags: Lp(a) CHD stroke aortic stenosis heart failure PAD FH secondary prevention FOURIER ODYSSEY
summary: Causal for CHD and calcific aortic valve disease; associated with stroke, PAD and heart failure. Elevated Lp(a) increases risk in FH and remains a residual risk after statin or PCSK9 therapy. In ODYSSEY OUTCOMES, Lp(a) reduction with alirocumab was associated with lower events independent of LDL-C (post hoc/prespecified analysis; modest absolute Lp(a) fall).

title: Managing elevated Lp(a); measurement; therapies
tags: Lp(a) measurement nmol/L mg/dL apheresis PCSK9 niacin antisense siRNA
summary: Measure Lp(a) at least once (EAS 2019). Prefer particle-concentration (nmol/L) assays; threshold ~>100 nmol/L (~50 mg/dL) in Caucasian populations, with units not simply interchangeable. Management: optimise modifiable risk factors; lifestyle barely changes Lp(a); PCSK9 mAbs lower ~15-30% (off-label for this purpose); apheresis effective in extreme cases; antisense/siRNA agents in outcome trials at the time of the text. Statins do not lower Lp(a).

title: Triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and remnant cholesterol
tags: remnant cholesterol TRL non-HDL apoB residual risk nonfasting
summary: Residual ASCVD risk on statins is linked to triglyceride-rich lipoproteins. Remnant-C = TC - LDL-C - HDL-C (calculated at no cost). The cholesterol, not triglyceride content, is the likely atherogenic factor; TG itself drives pancreatitis risk. Non-HDL-C and apoB capture remnants; nonfasting profiles are acceptable.

title: Risk with hypertriglyceridaemia; pancreatitis
tags: triglycerides pancreatitis MI stroke aortic stenosis 440 mg/dL
summary: TG >440 mg/dL (5 mmol/L) vs <88 mg/dL is associated with ~5x MI, ~3x ischaemic stroke, ~2x all-cause mortality and ~10x acute pancreatitis; absolute MI events far outnumber pancreatitis events.

title: Familial chylomicronaemia syndrome (type I)
tags: FCS chylomicronemia eruptive xanthoma lipaemia retinalis volanesorsen pancreatitis
summary: Suspect with TG >1000 mg/dL or eruptive xanthomas; usually secondary (obesity, diabetes, CKD, third-trimester pregnancy) first. Prevalence ~1 in 1 million. Pancreatitis is the main morbidity. Treatment: very low-fat diet (<15% fat) with dietitian; volanesorsen (apoC-III antisense) approved in Europe per textbook; plasma apheresis in some countries.

title: Remnant hyperlipidaemia (dysbetalipoproteinaemia, type III)
tags: type III apoE2 palmar xanthoma tuberous xanthoma
summary: Needs apoE2/2 plus a second hit (obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, renal disease, oestrogen, alcohol). Palmar xanthomas are pathognomonic; tuberous/tuberoeruptive xanthomas at knees/elbows; premature ASCVD in up to half. Responds to diet, weight loss and cholesterol/TG-lowering drugs.

title: Lipid targets across UK, Canada, Europe, US (2016-2019 era)
tags: targets comparison NICE CCS ESC ACC non-HDL apoB
summary: Secondary prevention: ESC/EAS 2019 >=50% and <55 mg/dL, non-HDL <85, apoB <65; ACC/AHA 2018 >=50% and <70 mg/dL, non-HDL <100; CCS <77 mg/dL (2.0 mmol/L), non-HDL <100, apoB <80. Superseded in the US by the 2026 guideline.

title: Treatment of mild-moderate hypertriglyceridaemia
tags: TG statin fibrate icosapent ethyl omega-3 REDUCE-IT STRENGTH pregnancy lifestyle
summary: Correct secondary causes (diabetes, CKD, alcohol, TG-raising drugs). Lifestyle: weight loss, reduce refined carbohydrate/sugary drinks/alcohol. LDL-C lowering remains the primary drug approach; high-intensity statin lowers TG ~30%. Fibrates (IIb) for statin-treated patients at LDL-C goal with high TG. Icosapent ethyl 2 g twice daily for TG 135-499 on statin (IIa, ESC). Low-dose omega-3 (1 g/day) gave no benefit; STRENGTH (EPA+DHA 4 g) had no event effect. Third-trimester pregnancy: monitor TG; >1000 mg/dL needs dietitian-led fat restriction.

title: HDL: biology and why HDL-C is not a target
tags: HDL particle HDL-P efflux reverse cholesterol transport Mendelian niacin CETP AIM-HIGH HPS2-THRIVE
summary: HDL-C is an inadequate surrogate; low HDL-C often reflects high remnant/apoB-lipoprotein burden. Mendelian randomization does not support causality of HDL-C. HDL-raising trials (niacin, CETP inhibitors) did not reduce events; HDL-P and efflux capacity are more informative but not clinical targets. Lifestyle (exercise, no smoking, moderate alcohol) raises HDL-C.

title: Genetic low HDL-C disorders
tags: APOA1 ABCA1 Tangier LCAT LPL low HDL
summary: ApoA-I deficiency (premature atherosclerosis, xanthomas), ABCA1 (Tangier), LCAT deficiency (corneal opacity, anaemia, renal disease; not premature CVD) and LPL deficiency. Extreme phenotypes need biallelic variants.

title: HDL-directed therapies: infusions and mimetics
tags: ERN/LRPT AIM-HIGH Milano CER-001 CSL112 AEGIS apoA-I
summary: AIM-HIGH (niacin on statin, LDL-C <70) and HPS2-THRIVE (niacin/laropiprant) showed no vascular benefit and more adverse events with niacin. HDL infusion/mimetic studies (apoA-I Milano, CER-001, CSL112) are imaging/efflux-endpoint or ongoing; clinical benefit unproven.
